content:
# Judith Chapter 6 — Disagreement Log
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Summary
**Total Disagreements: 18**
Chapter 6 is primarily Holofernes' furious speech and the delivery of Achior to Bethulia. Disagreements center on register (how threatening to make Holofernes sound), idiomatic expressions, and theological vocabulary in the people's prayer.

---

## Disagreements

**1. v. 1 — Title of Holofernes**
- EMET: "chief-general of the army"
- LOGOS: "commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army"
- PNEUMA: "supreme commander of the Assyrian forces"
- SOPHIA ruling: "commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army" (LOGOS)

**2. v. 2 — "hired-men" / "mercenaries" / "hirelings"**
- EMET: "hired-men of Ephraim"
- LOGOS: "mercenaries of Ephraim"
- PNEUMA: "Ephraimite hirelings"
- SOPHIA ruling: "Ephraimite hirelings" (blends PNEUMA/EMET register)

**3. v. 2 — Deity reference in Holofernes' speech**
- EMET: "their God" (capitalized)
- LOGOS: "their god" (lowercase to indicate Holofernes' contempt)
- PNEUMA: "their god" (lowercase)
- SOPHIA ruling: lowercase "god" in Holofernes' mouth — theologically significant distinction

**4. v. 2 — "will send his power" vs. "will send forth his might"**
- EMET: "will send forth his might"
- LOGOS: "will send his power"
- PNEUMA: "will unleash his power"
- SOPHIA ruling: "will send his power" (LOGOS)

**5. v. 3 — "force of our horses" vs. "cavalry"**
- EMET: "force of our horses"
- LOGOS: "force of our cavalry"
- PNEUMA: "our cavalry"
- SOPHIA ruling: "our cavalry" (modern clarity)

**6. v. 4 — "mountains drunk with blood"**
- EMET: "mountains will be drunk with their blood"
- LOGOS: "mountains will be drunk with their blood"
- PNEUMA: "mountains will run drunk with their blood"
- SOPHIA ruling: "mountains will be made drunk with their blood" (preserves Greek passive idiom)

**7. v. 4 — "footprints will not stand" / "footsteps will vanish"**
- EMET: "their footprints will not stand before our face"
- LOGOS: "not even their footprints will survive before us"
- PNEUMA: "their footsteps will vanish before us"
- SOPHIA ruling: "not even their footprints will survive before us" (LOGOS)

**8. v. 5 — "hired-man" / "hireling" / "mercenary"**
- EMET: "hired-man of Ammon"
- LOGOS: "hireling of Ammon"
- PNEUMA: "mercenary hired out to Ammon"
- SOPHIA ruling: "hireling of Ammon" (LOGOS — consistent with v.2 ruling)

**9. v. 5 — "day of your iniquity" vs. "in your wickedness"**
- EMET: "in the day of your-iniquity"
- LOGOS: "in your wickedness"
- PNEUMA: "in your folly"
- SOPHIA ruling: "in your wickedness" (LOGOS — *adikia* = wickedness/unrighteousness)

**10. v. 6 — "iron of my army" — structural**
- EMET: "iron of my army and multitude of those serving me"
- LOGOS: "iron of my army and the multitude of my troops"
- PNEUMA: "iron of my soldiers and the spears of my forces"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS; PNEUMA adds "spears" not in source

**11. v. 7 — "hill-country" / "highlands"**
- EMET: "hill-country"
- LOGOS: "hill country"
- PNEUMA: "highlands"
- SOPHIA ruling: "hill country" (standard biblical geography term)

**12. v. 9 — "let not your face fall" idiom**
- EMET: "let-not your-face fall" (fully literal)
- LOGOS: "do not be downcast" (paraphrase)
- PNEUMA: "do not look so stricken" (paraphrase)
- SOPHIA ruling: "do not let your face fall" (preserves the idiom)

**13. v. 10 — "standing ready" vs. "standing at ready" vs. "standing in his tent"**
- EMET: "standing ready in his tent"
- LOGOS: "standing in his tent"
- PNEUMA: "standing at ready in his tent"
- SOPHIA ruling: "standing ready in his tent" (EMET — captures the Greek *hestēkotes*)

**14. v. 12 — "held them at bay" / "kept them at bay" / "prevented"**
- EMET: "held them at bay and prevented them from going up"
- LOGOS: "kept them at bay"
- PNEUMA: "pelted them with rocks, pinning them down"
- SOPHIA ruling: "kept them at bay with stones, blocking their ascent" (blends LOGOS/EMET)

**15. v. 13 — "went under the hill" vs. "slipped beneath the hill"**
- EMET: "went under the hill"
- LOGOS: "went under the hill"
- PNEUMA: "ducked below the ridge"
- SOPHIA ruling: "slipped beneath the hill" — mild vivification acceptable

**16. v. 16 — "young-men ran together" vs. "young men assembled"**
- EMET: "all their young-men ran-together"
- LOGOS: "all the young men assembled"
- PNEUMA: "all the young men crowded in"
- SOPHIA ruling: "all the young men assembled" (LOGOS — less vivid but more dignified)

**17. v. 19 — "lowliness" / "humiliation" / "misery"**
- EMET: "lowliness of our race"
- LOGOS: "humiliation of our people"
- PNEUMA: "our people in our misery"
- SOPHIA ruling: "humiliation of our people" (LOGOS — *tapeinōsis* = humiliation/lowness)

**18. v. 19 — "those-who-have-been-consecrated" / "those consecrated" / "those who belong to you"**
- EMET: "those-who-have-been-consecrated to you"
- LOGOS: "those who are consecrated to you"
- PNEUMA: "those who belong to you"
- SOPHIA ruling: "those who are consecrated to you" (LOGOS — *hēgiasmenōn* requires consecration language)
